Vijay Kumawat is a design graduate from NIFT Himachal Pradesh. He has worked with organisations and institutes including NID Gandhinagar, NID Bangalore, D'source – Ekalpa (MHRD, Government of India), GMR Group, Elite Techno Group (Formula One Racing Marshals), the Wacom Design Challenge, Vivaran/Tabledege, the Archaeological Survey of India, Action for India, GSEB, CII, Hyderabad Runners, Airtel, AICTE, and the National Stock Exchange report design.

name: Marsukola Kranthi Kiran
bio: Doctoral Scholar, Department of Design, IIT Hyderabad — documenting and preserving Gond cultural heritage through digital technologies.
fullBio:
Marsukola Kranthi Kiran is a doctoral scholar in the Department of Design at IIT Hyderabad. He holds a postgraduate degree in Mass Communication and Journalism from Osmania University. Coming from the broader Gond society of Adilabad, Telangana, he brings an emic perspective to his work on documenting and representing Gond cultural heritage.

His doctoral research, Documenting and Preserving Gond Cultural Heritage through Digital Technologies in Adilabad, Telangana, focuses mainly on Gond intangible heritage, particularly oral and performative traditions, while also looking at aspects of material and visual culture. He uses design-led ethnography and participatory approaches, working closely with community members and knowledge holders. His research explores how digital and new media can help document and preserve living traditions, while keeping community knowledge, cultural context, and representation at the centre of the work.

name: Yash Desai
bio: Visual Artist & Researcher | PhD Candidate, Department of Design, IIT Hyderabad.
fullBio:
Yash is a Baroda-based visual artist, researcher, and PhD candidate in Design at IIT Hyderabad. His practice operates at the intersection of painting, traditional photographic processes, and new media as a visual art language. Driven by an interest in image philosophy and time-based media, his research examines the importance of individual and cultural memory in shaping identity, preserving history, and understanding shared human experience. Through this lens, he aims to develop innovative pedagogies that offer new pathways to contemporary image-making.

He is an artist-in-residence with the UNIDEE Residency Program at Fondazione Pistoletto (Italy), supported by the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation (2026), and has previously held a residency at Space Studio, Vadodara. A recipient of the Hyundai Art for Hope Grant (2026) and the Jeram Patel Award, he was also a fellow exploring traditional Rudra Veena making. Yash has exhibited at venues including the Museum of the Future (Dubai) and the India Art Fair, taught at MSU Baroda and the World University of Design, and designed an artist book for Shri Jyoti Bhatt.

name: Nandit Pastariya
bio: Architect & Assistant Professor — Research Scholar, IIT Hyderabad, working on digital heritage and architectural education.
fullBio:
Ar. Nandit Pastariya is an architect and assistant professor working at the intersection of architectural education, heritage documentation, digital heritage, and human experience in the built environment. His current research explores how architectural intangible heritage, particularly Indian temple architecture, can be communicated through emerging digital and visual media to encourage deeper public engagement.

His academic interests include public engagement with heritage, photogrammetry, architectural documentation, AR/VR/XR, cinematic storytelling, and experiential learning. As an educator, he teaches architectural design, history, visual arts, photography, and digital applications, and has developed field-based and heritage-oriented learning initiatives that connect architectural education with direct observation and documentation.

Before academia, Nandit worked across architectural practice, project management, construction, BIM, and design management, giving him a practice-oriented approach to architectural education. His emerging research direction brings together heritage, technology, and storytelling, with an emphasis on moving beyond the preservation of monuments toward creating more accessible and meaningful ways for people to understand and connect with historic environments.

name: Rucha Deshpande
bio: Assistant Professor & Programme Co-Ordinator, MIT-WPU — PhD Scholar, IIT Hyderabad, working on generative AI, UX, and design education.
fullBio:
With 16+ years of experience spanning industry and academia, Rucha Deshpande works at the intersection of design practice, research, technology, and education. Her academic and teaching practice focuses on creating experiential learning environments that encourage critical thinking, creative confidence, systemic thinking, and innovation, enabling learners to connect design theory with real-world challenges.

Her research explores the intersection of generative AI, user experience, human behaviour, creativity and creative cognition, design psychology, and design education. Her work examines how emerging technologies, psychological perspectives, and human-centred approaches can influence creative processes, user experiences, and design learning.

She is committed to advancing design education that nurtures reflective practitioners, adaptive thinkers, empathetic researchers, and responsible innovators equipped to navigate complexity and shape meaningful futures.

fullBio:
Kashish is a design educator and researcher with a background in fashion and textiles, currently pursuing doctoral research in Design. With experience teaching fashion and textile design, she brings together design practice, pedagogy, and research to explore how design can engage with cultural and social contexts.

Her research interests lie at the intersection of design research, craft and textile heritage, intangible cultural heritage, and community-centred design. Her current research explores how Virtual Reality (VR) and emerging digital technologies can support the documentation, interpretation, and preservation of intangible cultural heritage, while creating immersive and meaningful ways for contemporary audiences to engage with cultural practices.

Malthurkar Ganesh Kumar joined the Design Innovation Centre as a PhD scholar in January 2024, supervised by Prof. Deepak John Mathew. His research explores art and design education, and STEM and STEAM education in Indian schools.

Before returning to academia, he spent over 20 years as a user experience specialist, working across ethnographic research, strategic design, information architecture, and usability testing for organisations including Boeing, Nike, Adidas, Carrier, Infosys, and Honeywell — most recently as Senior User Experience Consultant and User Experience Architect at Infosys. He holds 4 innovation patents in human-centered design and is a Certified Usability Analyst (Human Factors International).

He is also a practicing sculptor known as "Gannu", co-founder and VP of the Telangana Sculptors and Artists Association (TSAA), founder of InnoMission (bridging academia, industry, and government), and creator of ABCD (AnyBody Can Draw™) — an initiative making art accessible to everyone.

Salil Sahadevan is a research scholar with IIT Hyderabad and a Deputy Secretary at the University Grants Commission. He works on the alternative futures of higher education, combining regulatory experience with design research, strategic foresight, and speculative method. He writes regularly for The Hindu and Deccan Herald. He holds a doctorate in Strategic Management from the University of Kerala.

His current research asks what higher education looks like when it is not organised as a university: it maps alternative and emerging formations worldwide, studies six Emerging Learning Community sites in India through fieldwork, and uses futures methods to build scenarios for Indian higher education.

fullBio:
Raja Sekhar Donka is a multidisciplinary product designer, UX researcher, and visual storyteller on DIC’s lab team, applying interaction design and cognitive science to build intuitive digital experiences. His work spans research-driven UX design, rapid prototyping, and motion design across 2D, 3D, and AR/VR. His current work at DIC focuses on creating embodied digital heritage experiences using virtual reality to enhance the understanding of heritage sites.

He holds an M.Des in New Media Design from the National Institute of Design, Gandhinagar, and a PG Certificate in Visual Design & UX from IIT Hyderabad. His master’s project, Socratease, was a cognitive UX case study exploring how conversational, Socratic-method-inspired interactions can reduce confirmation bias in news consumption, developed through action research with 30+ participants. Before moving into UX, he spent several years as a motion and 3D designer across edtech and studio production — including Vedantu Innovations, Toppr Technologies, and Srushti Creative Studio — creating educational 3D content, AR-ready visuals, and VFX for film and commercial work.

title: Virtual Recreation & Digital Preservation of Cultural Heritage Temple Sites of Southern States of India
subtitle: Digital Preservation through 3D Printing and Virtual Reality for the Temple Architecture of Telangana
tagline: Reviving the built heritage of the Kakatiya dynasty through photogrammetry, AR/VR and 3D documentation.
description: Telangana is home to several magnificent built monuments that reflect the region’s rich cultural heritage. The essential features of the Kakatiya dynasty reflect the built heritage of the Warangal region. Warangal is the cultural capital of the Telangana state; in terms of historical importance and its unique architectural style, it has become a state heritage site.

The project seeks to address these challenges by exploring the use of technology towards the digital preservation of the tangible aspects of the built heritage of southern India. The project also seeks to revive ancient culture and heritage by developing a comprehensive digital heritage repository through systematic documentation and using advanced technologies such as 3D documentation and AR and VR creations of the built heritage of Telangana, India.

Use of Technology towards digital preservation of the built cultural heritage.
To identify and make an inventory of all the architectural elements found through documentation.
Identify methods to safeguard and promote the Tangible cultural heritage and revival of ancient culture.
To involve the local communities in preserving the heritage and the surroundings of the premises.
Interpretation of the sculptures, reliefs and architectural elements and motifs.
Representation through methods of design innovation and technological advancement.

title: Tangible and Intangible Cultural Heritage of Telangana: Visual Documentation and Design Intervention
subtitle: Preserving the Past, Sustaining the Future with Mixed Reality (VR/AR), AI, and Design Interventions
subtitle2: Virtual Walkthroughs of Legacy: Gond Tribe’s Cultural Heritage
tagline: Preserving the past, sustaining the future with mixed reality (VR/AR), AI, and design interventions.
description: Our project focuses on digitally documenting and preserving the tangible and intangible heritage of Telangana spanning landmarks like the Ramappa Temple and Warangal Fort, along with the diverse crafts, rituals, and traditions of its communities, including the Gond tribe of Adilabad.

By employing cutting-edge technologies such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and advanced material studies, this initiative aims to create a comprehensive digital repository that merges design, technology, and cultural memory.
objectives: Heritage Documentation: Digitally capture and reconstruct Telangana’s architectural, artistic, and cultural legacy.
Design & Material Innovation: Apply modern design thinking and research to revitalize traditional crafts while maintaining authenticity.
AI-Driven Insights: Use AI for data processing, analysis, and preservation strategy optimization.
Immersive XR Experiences: Develop 1:1 virtual walkthroughs and interactive museum spaces to engage global audiences.
outcomes: The project will result in a dynamic digital archive and Virtual Museum Walkthroughs showcasing Telangana’s tangible and intangible heritage through VR and AR. It also empowers indigenous communities by transforming heritage documentation into livelihood opportunities. By bridging tradition with innovation, the initiative establishes a replicable model for sustainable cultural preservation ensuring that the art, architecture, and stories of Telangana continue to inspire generations to come.

title: Integrating AI, AR, and VR in Learning Models and Their Impact
tagline: Studying whether VR, AR and AI can make school classrooms more interactive, experiential and technology-enabled.
description: The Design Innovation Centre (DIC) project titled “Integrating AI, AR, and VR in Learning Models and Their Impact” aims to study the feasibility and effectiveness of immersive technologies in transforming school education in Telangana, India. The project focuses on evaluating how Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can create interactive, experiential, and technology-enabled classrooms in government schools.

The study assesses the readiness of schools and teachers for adopting immersive technology, explores methods to integrate these tools into existing curricula, and analyzes their effect on student engagement, comprehension, and retention. Conducted through surveys, interviews, and classroom observations, the project is designed for scalability and may later be expanded to other states across India. The goal is to develop and implement a robust and adaptable framework for AR/VR-based education that enhances conceptual clarity, strengthens academic fundamentals, and improves students’ curiosity-driven learning.

The project emphasizes multidisciplinary collaboration, combining design, pedagogy, and technology to create future-ready education systems. It aligns with the vision of the Ministry of Education and NEP 2020 to integrate advanced technologies into mainstream learning. Ultimately, the initiative seeks to develop scalable, accessible, and effective immersive education models that democratize quality learning, inspire innovation, and redefine how students perceive and interact with knowledge in the classroom.

The project’s core focus areas include developing curriculum-based chapter plans, creating a VR/AR learning environment, and formulating flexible guidelines for teachers and students to ensure smooth integration into existing teaching systems. The workflow involves the integration of hardware, software, and project files, troubleshooting technical challenges, finalizing and launching a beta version, conducting primary testing, and refining the product based on user experience during initial school trials.

The design team developed the concept and visual architecture for an immersive STEM education interface, initially exploring 3D home-screen buttons and icons for interactive navigation. However, the focus was later streamlined toward specific learning topics to ensure clarity and deeper pedagogical impact.

One of the most significant milestones of the project is the creation of a working model prototype representing the first eighteen elements of the Periodic Table in a virtual chemistry lab. This interactive simulation allows students to visualize atomic structures, molecular bonds, and chemical interactions safely and immersively within VR. The prototype demonstrates how virtual learning can bridge the gap between theory and practice.

title: Urban Mobility - Investigating the Visual Safety Preferences and Acceptance of Urban Air Mobility (UAM) for Indian Passengers: A Digital Design and VR Validation Study
tagline: Understanding how Indian passengers perceive the safety, comfort, and design aesthetics of autonomous air taxis.
description: This Design Innovation Centre (DIC) project explores the future of Urban Air Mobility (UAM) in India by analyzing user perceptions, safety preferences, and design acceptance of autonomous passenger drones, also referred to as “Air Taxis” or eVTOLs (Electric Vertical Take-off and Landing vehicles).

Project focuses on developing a comprehensive interior design and user experience framework for next-generation aerial transport. Through digital modeling and Virtual Reality (VR) validation, the study aims to understand how Indian passengers perceive the safety, comfort, and design aesthetics of these autonomous systems. The project further includes the exterior design and configuration of eVTOLs, ensuring that both functional and emotional aspects of passenger experience are addressed within India’s evolving urban mobility landscape.

title: No Soil Farming through Aquaponics
tagline: Growing food without soil — a closed-loop fish-and-plant system for space-starved Indian cities.
description: With agricultural land increasingly scarce in India’s growing cities, the Design Innovation Centre’s Urban Aquaponics project is reimagining how and where food can be grown. The system creates a closed recycling loop: edible fish are raised in ponds, their nutrient-rich waste feeds vertically arranged crops, and the water is continuously refreshed to sustain both fish and plants without any external fertiliser.

What began as a first-stage prototype, built through collaboration among first-year BTech and BDes students at the Centre, has since evolved into a broader research effort that tests the system at three distinct scales: compact units designed for apartment living, mid-scale rooftop installations, and community park-scale systems currently in development. Each version addresses a different layer of urban India’s food security challenge, from individual households to entire neighbourhoods.

The high-nitrogen, continuously circulating water from the fish ecosystem enables plants to grow noticeably faster than in conventional soil-based systems, while eliminating the need for chemical inputs. It’s a project that started as a student-led experiment and has grown into a genuine model for how cities without spare land can still grow their own food, cleanly, efficiently, and sustainably.

title: Mid School-Level Art and Design Education: A Pedagogical Framework for Assessing Telangana’s Social and Tribal Welfare Fine Arts Schools
tagline: A culturally-responsive assessment framework for the fine arts schools of Telangana’s Social and Tribal Welfare Residential Educational Institutions.

researchers.role: PhD Alumnus, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

sections.title: Context & Research Need
paragraphs: A specialized Art and Design education in Telangana Social Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGSWREIS Fine Arts School, Malkajgiri) and Telangana Tribal Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGTWREIS Fine Arts School, Narsapur), while these specialized "dual curriculum" schools aim to students pursue democratize creative education and identified early talents along with regular academics (State Board), middle schools (ages 11–14) is pivotal for cognitive and 21st-century skill development. However, existing assessment models often rely on generalized metrics that do not fully capture the contextual realities or specific artistic competencies of these marginalized communities.

sections.title: The Gap

title: Designing the Design Skill Tree: Visualisation Tool for the Design Curriculum in India
tagline: Adapting the game-design "skill tree" into a visualisation tool for mapping and personalising design curricula in India.

researchers.name: Harikrishna (Elias) Manoj
researchers.role: PhD Alumnus, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

sections.title: Introducing the Skill Tree
paragraphs: Originally from game design, skill trees use visual interfaces (nodes and connections) to enable learners to identify current skill progression, plan ahead to develop specific abilities, recognise foundational "keystone skills" that unlock further development, and sequentially build proficiency over time. Learners identify current progress, plan specialisation pathways, and recognise foundational "keystone skills" that unlock further development.

A skill tree functionally displays progression of time invested into development across two axes, where the vertical axis represents depth of knowledge and the horizontal axis represents breadth, by tracing a linear path from the foundation point onwards, guided by the user interacting with the skill. Skill trees have rarely been explored in formal pedagogy as a form of adaptive curricula, providing opportunity for exploration in practicum.

Design education in India evolved from Western pedagogical models with formal design education arriving through the early 1960’s. While Indian design pedagogy emphasises project-based learning, studio work, and individual guidance, critical gaps still exist: career pathway ambiguity, disconnect between curriculum and market demands, lack of structured skill mapping, static curricula in dynamic environments, and challenges in student-guidance infrastructure.

sections.title: Research Scope & Findings — Specialisation Project 1: Literature Review (63 → 23 Relevant Studies)
paragraphs: Skill trees support progress-mapping, clarify acquisition pathways, and increase engagement in project-driven learning. With literature providing minimal empirical implementations in design pedagogy, no studies providing longitudinal data, and scalability being untested and unclear for open-curriculum BDes programs, the project describes a vast opportunity of information that can be identified in the field of Personal Adaptive Curricula through the effect techniques of the Skill Tree mechanic in formal pedagogy within design education as a domain.

sections.title: Research Scope & Findings — Specialisation Project 2: Student Validation (26 BDes Students)
list: Pathway Ambiguity Confirmed — Course choice confusion widespread.
Faculty Variation Impact — Delivery inconsistency affects expectations.
Support Gap Confirmed — Traditional mode insufficient for open curricula.
Skill Tree Acceptance — Positive student response to visualisation concept.

sections.title: Current Design Pedagogy Alignment
paragraphs: Integration with theories of Reflective Practice (Schön) through visual mapping enables assessment of skill position and growth, Project-Based Learning, Self-Directed Learning, Studio Learning Theory, and the Guild Apprenticeship Heritage — prerequisite pathways mirror traditional artisan training curricula structures, providing a vantage point for involved students, faculty and administrative stakeholders to visualise the direction of the curricular structure.
list: Curriculum Types & Positioning — Traditional Curricula (TC): current structure cannot adapt dynamically.
Competency-Based (CBC): focuses on skill mastery but one outcome.
Personalised Adaptive (PAC): real-time pathway adjustment with a focus on a predetermined outcome.

sections.title: Operationalising the Curriculum
paragraphs: Skill Trees can provide support as supplementary visualisation tools within a PAC–CBC hybrid model of curricula design. To operationalise curriculum as a nested hierarchy enabling granular skill mapping: Domain → Discipline → Field → Subfield → Course → Skill.

In practice this would prioritise the foundation to build on a design aptitude filter (i.e. UCEED, NID-DAT, NIFT-DAT, etc.), and entry into a design school. Interactions with the curriculum begin with the different Domains, categorised by the Stanford Design School (Real/Virtual/Mixed interactions with world), with Disciplines (Communication/Industrial/UX/Interaction design), Fields (Advertising/Publication/Narratives, etc.), to Subfields such as emerging specialisations (like Digital Promotional Design). Courses would nest under Fields and Subfields to allocate how Skills integrate across the curricula and where cross-sectionality engages.

sections.title: Future Scope and Integration
paragraphs: Traditional design curricula cannot keep up with AI, VR and new digital specialisations, nor provide clear pathways in open-elective systems, creating a strong case for adaptive, personalised structures. Skill trees support a hybrid PAC–CBC curricula by allowing skill-specific modifications and updates, giving students clear, visualised trajectories, embedding reflective practice, and creating a live feedback loop with industry.

With no real curriculum-level implementations and no longitudinal data, the scalability is untested. Benefits span multiple stakeholders: students gain clarity and agency, faculty gain explicit standards and refinement data, industry gains visibility into competencies, and institutions gain a framework aligned with the Design Education Quality Mark. Successful implementation will require more on-site research across different design curricular contexts, particularly within the larger Indian design education landscape where design engagement varies from six-month courses to four-year degrees.

sections.title: Limitations of the Study
paragraphs: Participants were only 26 BDes students from IIT Hyderabad, recruited via convenience sampling, so they do not represent the wider Indian design education context. Faculty, industry, and administrators were not involved, preventing cross-checking of student views with other stakeholders. The current skill tree prototype only analyses the BDes curriculum of IIT Hyderabad up to the second year; further large-scale development requires more time invested into the project.

title: Transforming Education through Virtual Reality in Indian Middle Schools in Telangana: Development and Testing Their Effectiveness
tagline: A quasi-experimental study evaluating VR and mixed reality for critical thinking and problem-solving in Telangana’s middle schools, with iHED and DAAD.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The effectiveness of virtual reality (VR) and mixed reality (MR) in building learning models for school education, creating AR/VR educational content, assessing school readiness for VR-based teaching, and exploring the role of VR in education.

This study examines the long-term impact of VR integration on students’ critical thinking and problem-solving skills in Telangana. Further, the research investigates how VR technology can be adapted to different learning styles. It aims to create VR-based curricula in various subjects. The objective is to enhance immersive and interactive learning in Telangana’s middle schools. This research will improve educational quality and prepare students for future challenges.

sections.title: Research Objective & Framework
paragraphs: The research framework will provide data-driven recommendations for policymakers and educators regarding VR integration in secondary education.
list: Assessing virtual reality feasibility and effectiveness in Telangana’s secondary schools.
Analyzing the impact on student engagement, performance, and cognitive growth.
Evaluating virtual reality adaptability to various learning styles.
Developing evidence-based recommendations for VR integration in education.

sections.title: Methodology
paragraphs: The methodology for this study employs a mixed-methods approach to evaluate the potential of Virtual Reality (VR) in middle-school education in Telangana, India. A survey of participating students found: Gender identification — 59.1% female, 40.9% male. Technology awareness — 77.3% yes, 18.2% no, 4.5% unsure. Technology willingness — 90.9% yes, 9.1% no. Willingness to use VR/AR to learn subjects — 63.6% yes, 27.3% no, remainder not sure / definitely not.

sections.title: Study Design & Outcomes
list: Research design: Quasi-experimental with pre-test and post-test measurements.
Sample: Select and assign comparable schools to experimental (new methods) and control (traditional) groups.
Intervention: Implement VR content and train teachers in the experimental group.
Data collection: (a) Quantitative — pre-tests, post-tests, and ongoing performance data; (b) Qualitative — interviews and classroom observations.
Analysis: Compare test results, analyze performance trends, and conduct thematic analysis. Develop VR educational content.
Promoting equitable access to quality education: educational technology can help students across different socioeconomic backgrounds in Telangana’s middle schools.
Preparing students with essential digital skills that are crucial to future academic and professional pursuits.
Enabling interactive and personalized learning: educational technology facilitates tailored learning experiences and interactive content, enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes.

sections.title: Future Direction
list: Scale the model for broader impact and develop adaptive learning systems to transform personalized education.
Conduct longitudinal studies to assess long-term effects on learning outcomes and metacognitive skill development.
Explore implications for curriculum design: teacher training and assessment methods, integrating the model into modern pedagogy.

title: Tangible and Intangible Heritage of Telangana: A Visual Documentation and Design Intervention
tagline: Documenting and safeguarding the traditions, crafts, and oral histories of the Gond tribe of Adilabad and Asifabad, Telangana.
venue: Fourth All India DIC Meet 2024, IIT Hyderabad

researchers.role: PhD Alumnus, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

sections.title: Research Brief
paragraphs: The Gond tribe, India’s second-largest indigenous group, has important historical and cultural significance in the erstwhile Adilabad district of Telangana. This project intended to explore and document their traditional practises, craft traditions, rituals, and oral traditions while preserving and promoting their rich culture using design intervention approaches. The project has opened up more prospects for tangible and intangible cultural heritage and ways to safeguard the rich cultural heritage of Gonds.

The framework established and implemented in this project can be adapted to document and safeguard cultural heritage in different regions of India. To combat the loss of cultural heritage, this project conducted comprehensive research and documentation in the Adilabad and Asifabad districts of Telangana State. A virtual museum walkthrough showcasing the rich legacy of the Raj Gonds has been created as one of the project’s salient achievements, with interactive instructional content enabling users to discover, study, and enjoy Telangana’s cultural heritage. An effort has been made to preserve the Gond tribe’s legacy for future generations by utilising scientific technologies for digital preservation and virtual reproduction.

sections.title: Objectives
list: To identify and make an inventory of all the artefacts found through documentation.
Recording oral histories towards understanding the intangible cultural heritage.
Identify methods to safeguard cultural heritage.
To involve the traditional bearers and practitioners in safeguarding traditional crafts.
Interpretation of their customs and characteristics.
Representation of heritage through methods of design innovation.

title: Autonomous Urban Air Mobility: Investigating the Visual Safety Preferences of Urban Air Mobility (UAM) Exterior Design for Indian Passengers
tagline: A digital design and VR validation study of how Indian passengers perceive the visual safety of autonomous air-taxi exteriors.

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Urban Air Mobility (UAM), understood as "Air Taxis" or autonomous eVTOL aircraft, is being explored as an opportunity for public transportation amid the rapid urbanisation of Indian cities. NASA projects up to 750 million UAM journeys per year by 2030, making safety a crucial aspect of the design of these vehicles. Reference exterior configurations studied include vectored-thrust designs (e.g. Lilium), lift-and-cruise designs (e.g. Archer), and wingless hoverbike-style designs (e.g. Ehang).
The study builds on the design of UAM and its human acceptance, drawing on user-centered design, human cognition and product semantics, and exterior design with safety perceptions.

sections.title: Research Question & Objectives
paragraphs: This study examines how passengers’ safety concerns can influence the way UAMs are designed.
list: To investigate the impact of the UAM exterior design and its elements on visual safety.
To identify a more secure and widely accepted exterior design model among the proposed designs.
To study the effectiveness of VR in relation to the perception of digital prototypes of mobility design.
To prescribe a digital design of UAM for Indian passengers with the perception of safety.

sections.title: Methodology — Practice-Led Research (PLR) Approach
paragraphs: Addressing the above-mentioned objectives, the methodology is led by Practice-Led Research, focusing on learning through practical activities (Cross, 1982). It involves three main steps: exploring existing knowledge, engaging in practice, and reflecting on the results (Kwok, Yu and Le Run, 2025). This method allows creators to integrate theory and practice effectively in virtual reality projects (Tariq, 2025).

sections.title: User Study with VR Method
paragraphs: Survey design used an online survey and an in-person VR method. The method uses a survey-based approach that includes various proposed UAM aircraft exterior designs for passengers to assess their preferences and acceptance. This was conducted in two phases: an online survey (n=344) and an in-person VR method (n=103) followed by a survey, using head-mounted displays and handheld devices. Qualitative data was collected to measure preferences for the design options by addressing the perception of safety during the survey.

The results suggest that the UAM design featuring covered propellers (Option B) is perceived as offering the highest level of visual safety, leading to the most user preference. Covered propellers on wings above the cabin (Option A) are also well received, whereas designs with propellers at a lower level without wings (Option D) are less favoured. This indicates that propellers mounted at lower levels of the cabin impact user preferences, while guarded propellers mounted above the cabin positively influence them.

sections.title: Design Development
paragraphs: Design exploration also drew on bio-inspired form studies (e.g. bee and insect wing/body structures) feeding into a nature-inspired UAM concept.

title: Digital Preservation of the Cultural Heritage of Telangana through 3D Printing and Virtual Reality
tagline: Using 3D scanning, printing, and VR/AR to preserve Telangana’s built heritage without altering the physical structures.

sections.title: Research Brief
paragraphs: Built monuments have a significant contribution to forming an identity. They also serve as an essential aspect of cultural heritage, symbolizing the power and identity of the rulers. As per the guidelines given by the UNESCO Convention for building and natural heritage, the conservation and preservation of cultural properties is an important aspect of safeguarding and transmitting their legacies to future generations.

With the help of technological advancement, systematic digital preservation can be done. Technologies such as virtual reality and augmented reality are tremendous experiences that can be incorporated to enhance the monumental virtual experiences of built heritage. 3D scanning, printing, and digital documentation can prove to be a step forward in preserving tangible cultural heritage. Presenting the structures in 3D printing and virtual reality spaces is excellent for promoting tourism in India.

sections.title: Objectives
list: To preserve the rich cultural heritage in India without altering the physical structures.
To create a digital repository of architectural elements.
To create a small-scale replica of monuments for museumization and educational purposes.
To raise awareness among the younger generation about our culturally built heritage.
To promote heritage tourism in India.

title: Virtual Museum Design Experience: Digital Heritage & Preservation of Gond Artefacts through 3D Printing
tagline: Photogrammetry-documented Dhokra artefacts of the Gond community, rebuilt as a walkthrough virtual museum and 3D-printed replicas.

researchers.name: Krishna Trivedi
researchers.role: PhD Alumnus, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

sections.title: Research Brief
paragraphs: The traditional Dhokra artefacts have been documented using photogrammetry for 3D documentation of the sacred artefacts of the Gond community. To overcome the limitations of existing museum display practices, a virtual museum and walkthrough experience have been created. The museum’s data can also serve as a digital repository of traditional artefacts. The 360-degree display experience will enhance the visual experience and knowledge regarding the importance of the objects in Gond culture.

Documented artefacts include Waghoba (the sacred totem of the Six Clan Gonds), Ghoda (a decorative artefact), and a ceremonial Lamp (a utilitarian artefact) — each taken through a 2D image → point cloud data → 3D mesh with texture → 3D image for VR → 3D-printed artefact pipeline.

sections.title: Objectives
list: To incorporate technological advancements in creating high-tech digital museum experiences.
To create a virtual museum of experiences and knowledge sharing beyond the location constraint.
To identify and make an inventory of all the artefacts found through documentation.
Representation of the cultural history of the Gond community through methods of design innovation and technological advancements.
